+---
+assignees:
+- claude-code
+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: '80'
+title: Four multi-fixture tests pass the 60 s time limit in a parallel `swift test` run on a loaded machine
+---
+## Why
+
+On 2026-10-04, with the machine load average at 30 to 62 on 32 cores (sourcekit-lsp index builds of other packages), a parallel `swift test` run failed these four tests with "Time limit was exceeded: 60.000 seconds":
+
+- `SessionResumeTests.replayFromStartSendsWholeMessageUpsertsWithTheLiveIds()`
+- `SessionResumeTests.aNewAgentReplaysTheMessagesWithTheIdsOfTheEarlierAgent()`
+- `CompactionReportTests.aResumeReplaysTheCompactionEntryAndTheEarlierMessages()`
+- `BuiltinCommandsTests.noBuiltinInvokesTheModelBackend()`
+
+HEAD 2f8aeff (no local source change) fails the same four tests in the same way. `swift test --no-parallel` passes all 737 tests.
+
+Measured time of one resume test: 1.4 s alone, 2.4 s with its suite (12 tests), 22.7 s with three suites (44 tests), more than 60 s in the full run (737 tests). The four tests in the 44-test run all ended at the same time (22.7 s). Each test makes two or more agent fixtures in sequence, and each fixture starts a CodeContext index pass and an embedding pass.
+
+## What to do
+
+- Find the shared resource or the CPU cost that makes these tests scale with the number of tests that run at the same time.
+- Make the tests pass in a parallel run on a loaded machine, with no sleeps and no larger time limit as the only fix.
+
+Found during ^fhwk6sn.
\ No newline at end of file

+comments:
+- actor: claude-code
+  id: 01m44dren44q16xn59vmdc7f2z
+  text: |-
+    Research: root cause found and measured.
+
+    - Baseline (load average 30 to 46 on 32 cores): the 44-test three-suite run (SessionResumeTests, CompactionReportTests, BuiltinCommandsTests) passed after 30.9 s, then 18.5 s. The resume tests end between 18 s and 29 s.
+    - `sample` of the test process: the hot frames are FSEvents RPCs to fseventsd. `FSEventStreamStart` (2103 samples) on cooperative threads, called from `ToolCatalog.composeCodeContext` -> `CodeContext.start()` -> `Watcher.start()` -> `FSEventsFileEventSource.start`. `dispose_f2d_private_port` / `f2d_unregister_rpc` (5882 samples) on the `FoundationModelsCodeContext.watcher` queues after each stop.
+    - Experiment 1: the same run with the code context off in `composeCodeContext` (temporary env switch, now removed): 44 tests passed after 1.3 s (load average 46). Each of the four named tests took 0.86 s to 1.3 s.
+    - Experiment 2: the code context on, the embedder off: 27.8 s. Thus the embedding pass is not the cost.
+    - Experiment 3: a stand-alone program that starts N FSEvents streams at the same time, on this machine: N=1 takes 0.1 s to 0.3 s; N=10 takes 9.5 s (mean 5.5 s for each start); N=40 takes 13 s. fseventsd serves the stream registrations one at a time for the whole system. Thus each agent fixture that opens a session waits in the fseventsd queue behind all other tests (and behind the other processes of the machine), and a test that makes two or more fixtures in sequence waits two or more times. This is the shared serial resource.
+    - The unit fixtures do not use the code context: no session-level unit test calls a `tools.code_context` verb. `ToolCatalogTests` tests the code context through `ToolCatalog` directly. `SkillsLibraryTests` already turns it off.
+    - Fix plan (this repository only): `makeStubAgent` gives the agent a defaults layer (the `CODING_DEFAULTS_DIR` key of the injected environment, which `DotfolderStack` reads) whose `config.yaml` turns `tools.codeContext` off. A test that needs the code context can turn it on in its project layer.

   timestamp: 2026-10-04T21:40:13.092646+00:00
+- actor: claude-code
+  id: 01m44fejk34xttr5zq1rqxjr4f
+  text: |-
+    Implementation landed (no production code changed; test support and tests only).
+
+    1. `makeStubAgent` (`Tests/FoundationModelsACPAgentTestSupport/StubProfileFixtures.swift`) gives each stub agent a defaults layer through the injected environment key `<NAME>_DEFAULTS_DIR`, which `DotfolderStack` reads. Its `config.yaml` is `tools: codeContext: false`. New public `StubAgentDefaultsLayer.makeEnvironment(name:base:)`. A test that needs the code context through an agent can turn it on in its project layer.
+    2. The CLI composition suites (`AgentCompositionTests`, `AcpCommandTests`) compose over the new `ComposedPromptFixture.makeStubEnvironment(configHome:)`, which adds the same layer. Before: these 4 tests took 8.7 s alone (6 code contexts in sequence). After: 0.42 s.
+    3. New RED-then-GREEN tests: `HarnessSmokeTests.aStubAgentSessionStartsNoCodeContext()` and `AcpCommandTests.aSessionOverTheStubEnvironmentStartsNoCodeContext()`. Each failed first on `entry.surface.codeContextStop == nil`.
+    4. After fix 1, the full run is 10 times shorter, so all tests run in the first seconds, and `ToolsDoctorTests.aProberThatDoesNotAnswerInTimeWarnsInsideTheNamedTimeout()` failed 2 of 3 runs on `elapsed < 2 s` (2.54 s, 2.55 s, 8.2 s). It measured how long the loaded cooperative pool took, not the doctor. `ProfileDoctorTests.aResolverThatDoesNotAnswerInTimeWarnsInsideTheNamedTimeout()` has the same shape. Both now prove the timeout by order: the silent probe waits on a new `LateAnswerGate` (ignores cancellation) that the test opens only after `runHealthChecks()` returned; a doctor that waits for the probe never returns and the `.timeLimit(.minutes(1))` fails it. No sleep, no larger bound.
+
+    Measurements (load average 18 to 46 on 32 cores):
+    - 44-test three-suite run: before 30.9 s / 18.5 s; after 1.26 s. The four named tests: 0.83 s, 0.84 s, 0.87 s, 1.26 s.
+    - Full parallel run at HEAD: 737 tests, failed after 102.7 s with 18 time-limit failures (the four named tests and 14 more). After: 739 tests passed after 11.8 s; the four named tests 3.9 s to 4.4 s.
+
+    Discovered work, recorded as new tasks: ^00myfrq (direct `ToolCatalog` unit tests start a code context they do not need and never stop it; they are now the slowest tests, 9 s to 12 s) and ^bdzygnn (report upstream: `Watcher.start()` calls `FSEventStreamStart` on a cooperative thread).
+
+    Note: one edit in `AcpCommandTests.swift` was made with `sed` (a mechanical replace of three call sites); the result was checked.
